picks.forKenny: Target — this is the RB2 juice you asked for: a real 15-touch lead role, not a handcuff lottery ticket. Bid ahead of the one-week Shipley rental.
picks.name: Emanuel Wilson
picks.why: Seattle's lead back with rookie Jadarian Price (chest) on IR: 24 touches for 120 scrimmage yards and 2 TDs vs the Chargers in Week 4. Charbonnet (knee) isn't back yet, so Wilson should hold a 15-touch role against the 49ers.

picks.forKenny: Target — it's D.J. Moore's shoulder (not Baltimore's Chris Moore) opening real targets from Josh Allen; an upgrade on Wan'Dale's low-ceiling Titans role.
picks.name: Keon Coleman
picks.why: Career game (6 catches, 116 yards, 1 TD on 7 targets) after D.J. Moore's shoulder injury; 217 yards through 4 games at 15.5 YPR. Moore could miss 1-2 weeks with a Week 7 bye looming, making Coleman a WR3 rental with a growing every-week role.

picks.forKenny: Watch — your own rule: a backup who isn't good is a 5% flier at most. Let someone else pay $8 for a concussion-protocol rental.
picks.name: Dohnte Meyers
picks.why: 7 catches for 82 yards on 9 targets as Joe Burrow's de facto WR1 with Ja'Marr Chase (concussion) and Tee Higgins (adductor) sidelined. Former CFL standout with almost no NFL track record — pure injury rental, talent unproven.

picks.forKenny: Target as a one-week rental if you need a Week 5 RB — don't confuse him with a season-long answer.
picks.name: Will Shipley
picks.why: Only healthy RB on Philly's roster with Saquon Barkley (hamstring) week-to-week and Tank Bigsby (abdominal) on IR. Likely leads the backfield Sunday at Jacksonville; Dameon Pierce is the backup bid.

picks.forKenny: Skip — you have Trey McBride; don't spend FAAB on a second tight end.
picks.name: T.J. Hockenson
picks.why: 13 catches for 119 yards on 13 targets with Justin Jefferson sidelined; 22 catches for 195 yards through four games. Jefferson's eventual return caps the ceiling, but this is TE1 usage at the thinnest position.

picks.forKenny: Watch — committee back behind a workload-managed rookie; your bench already has Gordon and Monangai in this mold.
picks.name: Tyler Allgeier
picks.why: 8 carries for 42 yards and a TD vs the Giants as rookie Jeremiyah Love's workload gets managed (ankle). TD-dependent committee back, but the goal-line role is real.

picks.forKenny: Watch — only relevant while A.J. Brown sits; you're already stacked at WR with Collins back.
picks.name: Romeo Doubs
picks.why: 6 catches on 9 targets for 58 yards and 2 TDs vs Buffalo with A.J. Brown sidelined; 203 yards through four games on rising usage. Drake Maye is dealing.

picks.forKenny: Watch — fun PPR bench piece, but he doesn't solve your RB2 problem.
picks.name: Keaton Mitchell
picks.why: 15 touches (10 carries for 39 yards, 5 catches for 24) in Week 4 after 11 opportunities in Week 3 — trending up as a PPR satellite back for the Chargers. Explosive but not a lead role.

picks.forKenny: Target ONLY if the Rodgers claim fell through — Mahomes is on bye and this is the week's cleanest one-week stream.
picks.name: Jacoby Brissett
picks.why: Best widely available streamer: gets Detroit's worst-ranked pass defense in Week 5. Threw 2 TDs (with 3 INTs) in the Week 4 loss to the Giants; pure bye-week fill-in.

picks.forKenny: Skip — McBride is your guy; Strange is for managers streaming through byes.
picks.name: Brenton Strange
picks.why: 7 catches for 95 yards breakout vs Cincinnati with at least 2 receptions in every game — a real floor at a position with none. Not a star, but startable during byes.
